date_note: Berliner Zeitung (26 Nov) says Deichmann's customer notice is dated Tuesday 24 November; the other pages give only 25 November.
title: Deichmann says hackers accessed customer data in its online shop; Snipes also affected
summary: Unknown hackers accessed customer data in Deichmann's online shop, per Der Spiegel (via UA.NEWS) and dpa. Deichmann says names, addresses, invoices, email addresses, and phone numbers may be affected, but not passwords, account access or card numbers. It says it closed the vulnerability, informed authorities, filed a criminal complaint and has no signs of misuse. APA says Austrian customers were informed; dpa says Snipes is also affected.
plain: Deichmann says hackers accessed some customer data in its online shop. It says names, contact details, and invoices may be affected, but not passwords or card numbers.
exec: Deichmann reports unauthorised access to customer data in its online shop; it says it closed the vulnerability and has no signs of misuse.
action: As Deichmann advises, check the sender of unexpected messages and compare payment demands with your invoices; the company says its bank details have not changed and it never asks for passwords or payment data by email, phone or SMS.

validation.note: UA.NEWS (relaying Der Spiegel) and Marktspiegel/vol.at (dpa, APA) each state Deichmann's statement; Deichmann's own notice was not read.

review.note: stronger than source: removed 'chosen payment method' not on any page read; date moved to 24 Nov per notice dated Tuesday (Berliner Zeitung)
